en.title: Hideki Kamiya says game preservation matters more to him than whether games are physical or digital
en.description: The Clovers co-founder buys games digitally, but wants companies to ensure older titles remain playable
en.fullContent:
The Clovers co-founder buys games digitally, but wants companies to ensure older titles remain playable

Okami, Devil May Cry, and Bayonetta creator Hideki Kamiya says he’s more concerned about the future of game preservation than whether games remain available physically or digitally.

Speaking alongside fellow Clovers co-founder Kento Koyama, Kamiya shared his thoughts with VGC over the impending end of physical game discs on PlayStation platforms.

Kamiya said that while the news doesn’t particularly affect his own buying habbits, since he now buys games “100% digital”, he does fear that something meaningful will be lost when physical games disappear.

“I don’t buy a single physical game these days – every single game I buy is 100% digital,” he said, “so I look at that decision and think, ‘Yeah, I guess this is where things were heading’.”

As a keen retro games collector, Kamiya said his bigger concern is whether games will remain available to play as hardware and distribution platforms change.

en.title: ‘Ruin and decay bring a chance of rebirth’: Hidetaka Miyazaki on uniting players in a damaged world
en.description: As FromSoftware’s new multiplayer game The Duskbloods nears release, the legendary game director behind Dark Souls talks connection, pessimism and ...
en.fullContent:
As FromSoftware’s new multiplayer game The Duskbloods nears release, the legendary game director behind Dark Souls talks connection, pessimism and of course, feet

Since 2020’s Demon’s Souls, Japanese video game director Hidetaka Miyazaki has shown the world a different way to think about game design. His games defy convention with punishing fights, obscure rules, and unknowable, inhospitable worlds. The “Soulslike” genre – named after Demon’s Souls and its sequel Dark Souls – is now ubiquitous, influencing multimillion-sellers from God of War and Star Wars: Jedi to Hollow Knight. Miyazaki’s most recent success, 2022’s Elden Ring, which credited Game of Thrones author George RR Martin as a co-creator, sold over 30m copies and inspired Alex Garland to adapt it for the big screen at A24. It earned Miyazaki a spot on Time magazine’s “most influential” list, an accolade he shares with just one other game developer: Mario creator Shigeru Miyamoto.

Miyazaki is now 51 and has been FromSoftware’s president since 2014, elevated from game designer to CEO after the success of the Souls series. He has a cherubic face that could pass for 35. He rarely speaks publicly, and never on camera. When he does speak, he answers questions like one of his characters – softly, sadly, his head bowed, making eye-contact only when I am speaking. Outside the studio where we speak is the sprawl of Tokyo’s Shinjuku, an ever-changing maze where tourists get lost and pop-up stores appear and vanish without a trace. Today, a J-pop band performs in the square as the cicadas scream from the trees. A gilded statue of Melania, one of Elden Ring’s toughest bosses, looms over this dimly lit conference room inside From’s headquarters, a bonfire checkpoint away from the chaos.

FromSoftware’s in-game universes are filled with clues – enemies, places and scraps of information from item descriptions paint a vague image of the world, and the player fills the blank space. You never fully understand these domains, although countless YouTube video game theorists have tried – as have other developers in awe of his work. “Of all the many things Miyazaki and his team do well, creating a sense of mystery is the greatest,” explains Dishonored director Harvey Smith, who has more than 40 days’ playtime in Elden Ring. “It’s so incredibly hard to do in video games, which are technical systems … But Miyazaki somehow creates an atmosphere of wonder. Even when finishing, you are left ruminating on fun, murky elements that feel half understood. It’s a delicious sense of intrigue.”

Rather than the single-player action game that Miyazaki’s audience craves (fans are desperate for a sequel to his 2015 gothic masterpiece Bloodborne, for instance), his latest project The Duskbloods is a multiplayer Switch 2 exclusive. Eight players face off against ghoulish horrors, fighting each other to avoid being culled at the end of each round. The survivors are whittled down over three phases culminating in a final three-way battle. The Duskbloods is releasing to an audience with shifting tastes and trends, and it is certainly a risk. “I’m very nervous,” Miyazaki says. “With every title we release there is this mounting tension.”

The game opens with an arresting image: one hand reaching out for another. A male character is slumped on a chair, dejected; the shot moves in close to focus on their draped fingers. From below the frame, a pale hand slowly reaches out and caresses them before gently clasping his wrist. Hands are a recurring motif in Miyazaki’s games; in Elden Ring, massive crawling hands burrow up from underground to attack you, and hand-like giants are revered as deities.

en.title: ‘The Blood of Dawnwalker’ Is a Bloody Balm for My Completionism
en.description: I drink the blood of my fourth rat tonight. It’s only got so much life to give, so as soon as I drain it, I know I'll need to feed again. My hunger...
en.fullContent:
I drink the blood of my fourth rat tonight. It’s only got so much life to give, so as soon as I drain it, I know I'll need to feed again. My hunger is not fulfilled. My health bar is only half full. I need more blood. Now.

I toss the rat away as my glowing eyes flicker to another, just across the street. I bare my sharp, bloody teeth, turn into a cloud of shadow and bats, and teleport to my unsuspecting prey. I bite down hard. It’s too late to realize my target has changed. As I swarmed, a human city guard happened to walk right in front of me. My teeth sink into his throat instead. I could let go, but I do not. I drink, drink, drink. Then he falls to the ground. Dead. I wipe my mouth as the last rat scurries away into the dark.

“Well, I guess I’m going to Hell anyway,” my character quips.

The Blood of Dawnwalker is a vampire simulator and role-playing video game that launches today. It’s a dark adventure where you play as the titular Dawnwalker—human by day, monstrous vampire at night.

You can’t talk about The Blood of Dawnwalker without talking about The Witcher 3. They’re both third-person monster-slasher video games starring handsome protagonists with cool scars on their faces, both made by some of the same people.

Konrad Tomaszkiewicz, a former director at the Polish game studio and Witcher developer CD Projekt Red, was one of three directors of the very popular The Witcher 3. His new studio, Rebel Wolves, even feels like a cheeky nod to Geralt, the main character of The Witcher series who is often called the White Wolf. The gameplay and graphics feel very similar. Combat involves swinging your sword and blasting magic abilities, while cutscenes and dialog have familiar dialog trees and quick-time events. You have a special sense that makes important items glow so you can find footprints and track down monsters.

en.title: Malick Fofana: Private jets, video games and an unlikely tug of war between Sunderland and Palace
en.description: Malick Fofana ended up joining Sunderland on deadline day Olivier Chassignole/AFP via Getty Images
en.fullContent:
Malick Fofana ended up joining Sunderland on deadline day Olivier Chassignole/AFP via Getty Images

Malick Fofana became an unlikely main character on Tuesday’s transfer deadline day. The 21-year-old Belgian winger left Lyon to join Sunderland for £30million ($41m), but only after one of the sagas of the summer.

It involved a fleet of private jets, competing stories of simultaneous medicals, and a classic game of Premier League one-upmanship that ran throughout the day, while the player sat at home, playing computer games.

Firstly, the footballer: Fofana has established himself as one of the most talented young forwards in France. He joined Lyon from Gent in 2024 and in the two seasons that followed, showed himself to be a dynamic, dangerous ball carrier and a versatile attacking weapon.

Premier League interest naturally followed and Fofana, who has five international caps for Belgium but was not part of the recent World Cup squad, has been a regular in gossip columns for much of the past year.

That made sense. The Belgian and French markets have been areas of focus for the club, particularly over the past 12 months. Before Fofana, Sunderland had already signed three players (Dayann Methalie, Thomas Meunier and Jules Ahoka) from those leagues this summer. This time last year, as the Black Cats prepared for their first season back in the Premier League, it was four.

en.title: 'GTA 6' on PS5 vs Xbox: Key differences to consider
en.description: Grand Theft Auto VI launches on Nov. 19 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series consoles. As far as anyone knows, it could be years before there's a PC ve...
en.fullContent:
Grand Theft Auto VI launches on Nov. 19 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series consoles. As far as anyone knows, it could be years before there's a PC version of the hotly anticipated open-world crime game (fortunately, we don't think it will take that long). But if you want to play the game right away, then it's time for you to figure out which version to buy.

After pre-orders opened, IGN reported that PS5 versions of the game were outselling Xbox at an eight-to-one ratio. Microsoft denied these numbers, of course, but if IGN's readers are representative of gamers as a whole, then players are certainly leaning in a very clear direction.

So, should you play GTA 6 on PS5 or Xbox? There are a lot of variables that make this a difficult question to answer. That said, we're going to do our best. Here is everything you need to know before buying GTA VI on PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series S/X

The first thing to note here is that the only official gameplay footage we've seen of GTA 6 comes from a 26-minute extended look released on Netflix in late August. It lived up to the hype, but less than half an hour of carefully curated footage is not a great way to determine the technical ins and outs of a video game.

It's also worth pointing out, though, that the Netflix footage was captured on PlayStation 5. Sony has even said in its marketing that the game "plays best on PS5."

"Thanks to the close partnership between Sony Interactive Entertainment and Rockstar Games, Grand Theft Auto VI will play best on PS5 by taking advantage of PS5’s immersive features to deliver a deeply engaging single-player experience when it launches on November 19," a Sony blog post reads.
